dashboard_line: B2 provisioner + immutable backup designed; 1 Terraform template; 8 edge cases handled
prescan_decision: passed — no prior admin-provisioning-design-w2 artifacts found in manifests/2026-04-28/

artifacts.description: 0x_b2_provisioner.py — idempotent WORM bucket provisioner with exponential+jitter backoff, scoped credentials (write+read-only), Terraform HCL output, COC integration, COMPLIANCE-mode lifecycle (forensics/=WORM, pollen/=versioning, temp/=90d-delete), dry-run support

0x_immutable_backup.py — idempotent tar.gz snapshot creator with SHA-256 hashing, B2 WORM upload, delete-test immutability verification, COC provenance chain logging, backup manifest JSON, recovery instructions, force-new override

success_criteria_check.idempotency_mechanism: bucket existence pre-check via b2_list_buckets; content-hash check via b2_list_file_names on same-day bucket
success_criteria_check.credentials_mechanism: env var precedence chain: B2_KEY_ID > BACKBLAZE_KEY_ID > B2_MASTER_KEY_ID; never hardcoded; CI/CD variable compatible
success_criteria_check.backoff_mechanism: exponential backoff with ±25% jitter; 6 attempts; cap 64s; covers 429, 503, 408, network errors
success_criteria_check.coc_mechanism: 0x_coc_writer.py auto-discovered from known locations; degrades gracefully if absent (exit code 4 warning)
success_criteria_check.error_handling_mechanism: structured exit codes 0-5; fail-fast on credentials/validation; retry on transient B2 errors; all errors logged
success_criteria_check.terraform_mechanism: single .tf file per bucket; uses backblaze/backblaze >= 0.8 provider; credentials as variables (never hardcoded); lifecycle rules wired

edge_cases_handled: Bucket name length enforcement (6-50 chars); truncation with preserved date suffix
Bucket already exists: idempotent reuse without duplicate creation
Identical backup content: SHA-256 hash comparison before upload (skip if same)
B2 rate limits (429/503): exponential backoff with jitter across 6 attempts
Network errors: retry with backoff, surface after 6 failures
Upload failures: per-chunk SHA1 verification per B2 protocol; retry on 408/429/503
WORM lock verification: probe-delete test (expect 403); non-fatal warn if unconfirmable
COC writer unavailable: silent degradation with exit-code-4 advisory (backup still succeeds)

features: terraform import command for existing buckets

ffff_analysis.findings: Two production-ready idempotent Python scripts designed; B2 provisioner handles full lifecycle from authorization through Terraform export; immutable backup handles snapshot creation through WORM verification. Both integrate with canonical 0x_coc_writer.py.
ffff_analysis.flags: WORM verification via delete-probe may be blocked by some B2 account configurations (Object Lock must be enabled at account level first — provider-level limitation, not script limitation). Rate-limit 40% failure in Phase 1 discovery is addressable by the exponential+jitter implementation.
ffff_analysis.flow: provision_worm_bucket() → b2_authorize() → b2_find_bucket() → [create if absent] → b2_create_worm_bucket() → b2_verify_worm_immutability() → b2_create_scoped_key(write) → b2_create_scoped_key(read) → write_terraform_config() → log_to_coc(). Parallel flow: create_immutable_backup() → create_tar_snapshot() → [find/create bucket] → [idempotency hash check] → b2_upload_file() → b2_verify_immutability() → log_to_coc() → write_manifest_json().
ffff_analysis.friction: B2 Object Lock (WORM) requires account-level enablement (B2 Plus/Enterprise or support request). Scripts gracefully warn when object lock not active rather than failing hard. Terraform provider version pinned to >= 0.8 which is current; may need update as B2 provider evolves.

positive_mutations: Enables WORM-compliant backup capability not previously possible in faerie-vault (new capability from script consolidation)
Dual credentials (write + read-only) pattern separates auditor access from write access — was not in original bash scripts
Content-hash idempotency check prevents duplicate uploads — original bash scripts would upload unconditionally
mysterious_mutations: Rate-limit backoff effectiveness: actual B2 response times under load are unmeasured; 40% failure rate from Phase 1 should drop but exact improvement ratio requires post-implementation measurement
